input.quote: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created (and paid for) by Customer and leaves Customer only a revocable, non-transferable licence limited to the Order Form term. That fails the fallback (no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, modifiable, sublicensable licence) and is far short of the preferred position, so it is a material deviation rather than a wording point. Sections 14.3 and 13.2 already preserve Vendor Technology and give Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables, 14.1 confirms Customer owns Customer Data, and 14.4 prevents joint ownership; the only other gap is the scope of Vendor's Customer Data rights, which in 14.1 extended to "improve the Services" and in 15.1 to uses "permitted by this Agreement" and to sale/advertising/model training with consent. We therefore flip ownership in 14.2 with an express assignment and narrow both data provisions to processing solely to provide the Services.

proposal.summary: Customer owns and Vendor assigns Deliverables; Vendor's Customer Data rights narrowed to processing solely to provide the Services
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we pay for, so we have flipped Section 14.2 to Customer ownership with an express assignment (Vendor keeps Vendor Technology under 14.3 and the embedded-IP licence in 13.2 is unchanged). We also narrowed Vendor's Customer Data rights in 14.1 and 15.1 to processing solely to provide the Services, removing the improvement and consent-based uses.
